title: TRACE: Efficient Transfer Learning for Neural Whole-Body Control Across Humanoid Embodiments
subtitle: Transfer the motion knowledge. Adapt the body.
summary: From Unitree G1 to full-scale H2: one adapted controller for dynamic motion tracking, whole-body teleoperation, and downstream VLA tasks.
authorNote: The current manuscript has an empty author field. No author names or affiliations are inferred.
abstract: Humanoid behavior foundation models enable diverse whole-body control, but transferring a pretrained controller to a new body requires handling changes in kinematics and dynamics. TRACE preserves the pretrained motion representation while adapting feedback control to the target robot. It combines kinematic priors and nominal joint-response alignment with encoder distillation and low-rank reinforcement learning on a compact motion set. A two-phase curriculum first establishes stable tracking, then refines difficult motions. Transferring SONIC from Unitree G1 to Unitree H2 takes approximately eight hours on a single RTX PRO 6000 GPU using 10 million motion frames. The adapted controller achieves 96.08% success on 67,953 evaluation motions under a height-scaled tracking criterion, and supports dynamic motion tracking, teleoperation, and downstream VLA applications on physical H2 hardware.

metrics.label: Single-GPU adaptation
metrics.detail: One RTX PRO 6000; adaptation from the released SONIC checkpoint. Source pretraining is excluded.

metrics.label: Motion frames
metrics.detail: A curated BONES-SEED transfer set with paired G1 and H2 references.

metrics.label: Motion-tracking success
metrics.detail: 67,953 held-out PHUMA motions in simulation, using a body-height-scaled success threshold.

method.title: Align the embodiment
method.description: Inject kinematic priors into reference, observation, and action projections. Align action scales and nominal joint responses before target-side fine-tuning.

method.title: Curate a compact motion set
method.description: Retarget motions to both robots, screen physical validity, balance motion categories, and select diverse commands using frozen source-model descriptors.

method.title: Separate representation and control
method.description: Distill source command latents and tokens into the target encoder while PPO adapts the control decoder through low-rank branches. A two-phase curriculum progresses from broad, stable tracking to difficult motions.

method.title: Reuse one motion interface
method.description: Deploy the same adapted low-level controller for reference-motion tracking, VR teleoperation, and downstream VLA tasks on the physical H2 robot.

benchmark.name: PHUMA motion tracking
benchmark.note: Success requires root, wrist, and ankle world-height errors to remain within the threshold at every evaluated frame: 0.250 m for G1 and 0.3447 m for H2, scaled by body height. Errors are measured at 50 Hz on each policy's own successful-motion subset, so the error averages do not use identical motion sets.
benchmark.sourceComparison: SONIC/G1 is a source-controller reference, evaluated with references retargeted to its own embodiment. The experiment does not establish cross-robot superiority.

vlaBenchmark.name: VLA task success on physical H2
vlaBenchmark.note: These are the manuscript's five evaluation tasks. The v33 gallery is a separate qualitative selection and is not a one-to-one record of this benchmark. The presentation's separate 19/20 continuous-trial clip must not be used as an aggregate VLA success rate.

costNote: The manuscript's less-than-0.1% GPU-hour comparison uses SONIC's reported 21,000 GPU-hours as a reference. TRACE's approximately eight GPU-hours cover adaptation only, excluding source pretraining. GPU-hours are not normalized across hardware.
limitations: The evaluation covers one source model (SONIC) and one embodiment pair (Unitree G1 to H2).
Simulation success uses body-size-adjusted thresholds. Position and temporal errors are reported over each policy's successful motions only.
Training-curve comparisons use one run per method; they do not report variation across seeds.
Hardware motion examples are qualitative demonstrations; globally referenced tracking errors were not reliably measured on hardware.
Gallery task labels and benchmark task definitions are recorded separately.
